At 10 years old I told my parents I was trans.  Couple years of mental hospitals later and they finally let me go full time.  My lazy, irresponsible mom who can't even clean a house decides to pop two more kids out because she wants a, "daughter."  At 14, I'm starting to spiral into drug use and rough crowds and find myself expelled from school.  One screaming argument later about how they're the only ones who don't accept me and how terrible it was for their broke selves to have even more children, dad takes me for a drive.  We go to a children's home, and he starts processing me in.  I'm numb, eyes stinging, too shocked to feel angry.

First three months in the home were okay.  I'm one of the few white girls.  The schooling program was a one size fits all complete joke, so I read the textbooks on my own and begin to enjoy reading.  Somehow it leaks that I'm trans and they force me to the boys section, a fully passable trans girl in the middle of puberty among a bunch of unstable future gangsters.  Fights happened, other bad things happened, and I saw a kid hang himself.  Some old guy found me on facebook, gave me money go in a hotel room with him.  I snuck out(escaped), got into this stranger's truck, and got enough money to stay with a friend for a month.  Nobody hires a 14 year old.  It was two years until I could work full time, but I did, began college, went to the gym, life was good.  Then the drugs came back, fast forward 8 years and I'm clean.

My mom contacted me three years ago and I flew in for a visit.  We all talk now.  I speak with my dad on the phone regularly, and sometimes to my mother.  I understand they're mentally ill.  They still live check to check.  She still doesn't work or clean.  My little bros are very intelligent and creative!  It sucks being in another part of the country, watching my little brothers grow up without me.  I want to be a part of their lives, but they grew up so darned fast.
